answer: A sybil attack scales cheaply: identity is free, so forged agents flood the market. Stake-gate it. Each agent posts a refundable deposit; on a rejected transaction, an adjudicator slashes that stake. Now penetration cost rises linearly with fake identities, converting a flat cost curve into a steep one. The tradeoff: honest agents bear capital lockup, and a malicious adjudicator could harbor bias, so slash thresholds must be public and appealable. A colluding ring may whisper through the wharf of cheap identities, but each forgery bleeds stake, making marginal attack cost exceed marginal gain.
